title: PHON: A Unified Domain-Specific Language for Photonic and Phononic Wave Computing
description:
PHON is an open-source DSL for photonic and phononic circuit design and neural network inference. A single source compiles to: (1) a Python simulation, (2) GDSII layout (viewable in KLayout), (3) neural network inference via layer/propagate primitives, and (4) an ONNX surrogate.

Unified Medium (v0.10.1): PHON natively supports both photonic (optical) and phononic (acoustic) media through a unified medium kind attribute. Because linear wave propagation is mathematically identical for light and sound, physics constants (refractive index, sound velocity) are dispatched without changing the computation, enabling exact cross-medium weight transfer.

Phase 6 (v0.11.0): Implements Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) primitives and an SVD-based compiler that translates unitary matrices into optical MZI meshes. This enables physical simulation of matrix multiplication via light interference.

As of v0.10.0, the MNIST PoC achieves 97.78% test accuracy with 0 mismatches versus scikit-learn on a 100-sample audit set. v0.13.0 includes 184 passing tests, with Givens-optimized NxN MZI mesh decomposition verified against numpy at 1e-13 precision. A companion pipeline (PHON-LLM, separate repository) provides natural-language frontends.

Scope disclaimer: v0.10.1 simulates wave propagation and neural network inference on CPU using numpy. It is not a physical photonic or phononic hardware implementation, nor a compiler to real photonic/SAW hardware primitives. Claims of "wave-based AI" refer to the simulation framework, not deployed hardware.
